participants.note: Concept ACKed migration, but requested restructuring test cases to run independently, using integer amounts, and simplifying helpers
Concept ACKed migration; questioned TestSRDSuccess and agreed to review a separate PR for it
pointed out bugs in TestSRDSuccess, but agreed to address them in a separate PR

claims.text: Whether default_cs_params can be removed as well now
claims.quote: Here we can remove the `default_cs_params` as well now, right?

claims.text: Simplify the input equivalence helper using std::ranges::is_permutation or direct sorted comparison
claims.quote: The previous implementation was indeed hard to understand. This is basically a permutation check of a subset of fields, and since we have very few elements here (given it's test code), we could either

claims.text: Remove is_eff_value altogether since every caller uses effective values
claims.quote: Since every caller uses effective values, could we remove `is_eff_value` altogether?

claims.text: Helper assertions obscure test failure line numbers and prevent test scenarios from running independently
claims.quote: Assertions inside these helpers report the helper's source line, so test_title has to identify the individual scenario. Could we organize the scenarios into named Boost test cases and share the repeat

claims.text: Drop expected_amount, its accumulation, and its assertion since HaveEquivalentInputs already compares input values
claims.quote: `HaveEquivalentInputs` already compares the input values, and `GetSelectedValue()` just sums them. Could we drop `expected_amount`, its accumulation, and this assertion?

claims.text: Floating-point arithmetic followed by conversion to CAmount risks imprecision compared to integer satoshi amounts
claims.quote: Could we use integer amounts throughout the migrated tests, e.g. 33 * CENT here and 2'533 * CENT for the target below? This expresses the intended satoshi amounts directly and avoids floating-point mu

claims.text: Allow AddDuplicateCoins to take an optional input size so four loops become four helper calls
claims.quote: Could `AddDuplicateCoins` take an optional input size so these four loops become four calls to the existing helper?

claims.text: Build expected_inputs once and initialize utxo_pool from it before adding heavier clones to avoid duplicate coin constructions
claims.quote: We could also build `expected_inputs` once and initialize `utxo_pool` from it before adding the heavier clones, which avoids constructing the four expected coins twice.

claims.text: Clarify comment explaining input equivalence regardless of prevouts
claims.quote: Two results are equivalent if they are composed of inputs with the same amounts and sizes, even if they are composed from different outputs (i.e., different prevouts).

claims.text: Use real values for max_selection_weight like 400,000
claims.quote: This is a strange max_selection_weight. It would be better to use real values, like max transaction weight of of 400_000 I think, although that's unrelated to this change.

claims.text: Why a set and target of 40000 was chosen rather than 400000
claims.quote: Unrelated to this change, but why choose a set and target of 40000? I had thought at first this was 400000 which would make more sense, so I wonder if this was a typo.

claims.text: TestSRDSuccess uses utxo_pool instead of mixed_weight_pool, so the tie-break is not checked and passes even when #33223 is reverted
claims.quote: TestSRDSuccess calls utxo_pool instead of the mixed_weight_pool it builds. As a result, the tie-break test passes even when #33223 is reverted. There's nothing checking the tie-break.
claims.status_note: Zeegaths agreed to address this in a separate PR
claims.status_by_quote: sure, I have a draft; I wanted to check before opening a PR

claims.text: Coin eviction never happens in TestSRDSuccess because max weight fits any two coins
claims.quote: Also coin eviction never happens because the current max weight (804 WU) fits any two coins (544 WU).
claims.status_note: Zeegaths agreed to address this in a separate PR
claims.status_by_quote: sure, I have a draft; I wanted to check before opening a PR

claims.text: Whether TestSRDSuccess fails to test eviction because the target only takes two UTXOs to reach, and whether it should assert the resulting UTXOs on success
claims.quote: Looking a little closer at the test, I think there is more wrong than simply it should be `mixed_weight_pool` instead of `utxo_pool`.
claims.status_note: yancyribbens agreed to handle this in Zeegaths' separate PR
claims.status_by_quote: I will take a look if you want to open a PR to fix the test.

support.reason: It would be nice to see the coinselector test file removed entirely in the future since having multiple test files has caused confusion.
supports migration and provided branch with test simplification ideas

result.notes: Zeegaths agreed to open a separate PR for the TestSRDSuccess bugs, and yancyribbens agreed to review it there rather than holding up this PR, accepting both objections and the related question.
